literal: Under the protective umbrella of the king possessing the quality of bearing words that are bitter to the ear, the world will abide.
translation: The world will rest under the protective umbrella of a ruler who has the noble quality of tolerating words that are bitter to his ears.
modern: தன் காதுகளுக்குக் கசப்பாக இருக்கும் சொற்களையும் பொறுத்துக் கொள்ளும் குணம் கொண்ட அரசனுடைய குடையின் கீழ் இவ்வுலகம் தங்கி வாழும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of a ruler's tolerance toward criticism. The phrase 'cevi kaippa' means 'to make the ears bitter', referring to harsh but necessary truths or criticisms. A ruler who possesses the quality of patiently enduring such bitter words is highly revered. The 'kavikai' or protective umbrella represents the king's sovereign protection, and the poet states that the entire world will willingly seek shelter and abide under such a benevolent and tolerant ruler.
